newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Henderson Land net satisfactory - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Henderson Land net satisfactory - analysts.

text.p: Henderson Land Development Co Ltd produced satisfactory results in fiscal 1996 but earnings at its Henderson Investment Ltd unit were disappointing, analysts said.
Henderson Land reported net profit of HK$8.36 billion in the year ended June 30, up from HK$7.03 billion the previous year.
Net profit at Henderson Investment rose to HK$1.89 billion from HK$1.63 billion.
"I would characterise the results as steady set of results no cause for jubilation and they may cause some disappointment," said Franklin Lam, director of research at HG Asia.

"In each of past three years, Henderson Land had managed to spring major positive surprises on the market by either producing a much higher earnings number or by being very generous on the distribution side. This year it has done neither," he said.
He had expected Henderson Land to post net profit of HK$8.088 billion in the 1996 fiscal year. The company's final HK$1.43 dividend was in line with expectations, Lam said.
Analysts said Henderson Land had achieved 19 percent earnings growth during the 1996 fiscal year through the sale of major property developments.

"I would imagine that they have obtained probably slightly higher prices and probably a few more sales than was generally expected," said Andrew Taylor, analyst at Asia Equity. He had expected Henderson Land to report net profit of HK$8.13 billion.
"We saw quite significant growth in the first half of the year in residential capital value," Taylor added.

Lam said Henderson Land has benefited from high margin sales with its developments in the Mid-Levels. "A lot of these projects are property projects in the Mid-Levels. The margins were quite high," he said.
However, analysts said lower-than-expected property development earnings at Henderson Investment were probably responsible for the lower-than-forecast results.
"The short fall is probably due to less interest income and less property sales," said Desmond Cheung, analyst at Vickers Ballas. He was expecting net profit of HK$2.2 billion.
Taylor had forecast net profit of HK$1.94 billion. "I would imagine that that market would find that reasonably disappointing," he said of the final result.
Analysts noted that Henderson Investment shares had run up ahead of its inclusion in the Hang Seng index on August 30 and the stock could see some weakness.
Henderson Investment shares closed unchanged ahead of the earnings announcement on Wednesday at HK$8.15.
"At this kind of level it is not particularly attractive and we will be scaling back our recommendation on the stock from a buy to a hold," said Lam.
He said however that we was maintaining a buy recommendation on Henderson Land since he was bullish on the outlook for the residential property market for the next six to 12 months.
"But in the next month and a half there should not be anything exciting at all and that means that there may be some share price softness," he added.
Taylor said Henderson Land's fiscal 1996 results should provide support for the stock at current levels. "We may actually see it move higher tomorrow," he added.
Henderson Land shares closed at HK$61.00 on Wednesday, down HK$0.75.
Henderson China Holdings Ltd, a spinoff unit of Henderson Land, also reported its fiscal 1996 earnings on Wednesday. It posted net profit of HK$564.16 million compared to HK$21.0 million last year.
